messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: canary group 'inference-r1' exceeded abort thresholds (healthcheck fail rate 18%, 5xx spike). Auto-abort not triggered yet — notify oncall. https://monitoring/redwood/canaries/inference-r1 :rotating_light:
Maria: I'm on it. Seeing perf alerts + grafana panel, p95 latency jumped and kube restarts on a subset of pods. Paging SREs.
Devin: joining. Which deploy is this tied to?
Maria: rollout id=rl-2026-03-15-09, started 09:02 UTC. Canary = 5% traffic to inference-r1, now 5xx across 2/5 nodes.
Samir: looking at pod logs, getting repeated OOMKilled + "malloc: out of memory" in model-server process. Copying tail:
```
[2026-03-15T09:08:12Z] model-server[pid=4123]: ERROR runtime: allocation failed - returning 503
[2026-03-15T09:08:17Z] kubelet: Pod inference-r1-3 OOMKilled
[2026-03-15T09:08:18Z] liveness probe failed for container model
```
Joan: that's consistent with memory leak hypothesis. Did the package include a new runtime or changed batching?
Maria: yes, last change was switching batching strategy and bumping max_batch_size to 128 in rl-2026-03-15-09. Could blow up mem for long sequences.
Devin: quick impact note for PG team: ~4% of production requests saw 5xx in last 6m, mostly long-context completions. Might affect streaming clients + some webhook customers.
Samir: recommend immediate mitigation: 1) remove canary traffic weight 2) flip canary kill-switch flag 3) pin rollback if needed.
Maria: I'm going to flip the rollout kill-switch now. Command: `rbctl rollout abort rl-2026-03-15-09 --reason "canary OOMs/5xx"`
deploy-bot: `rbctl` started abort for rl-2026-03-15-09 by Maria. Steps: disabling traffic routing, signaling deploy-service, triggering rollback.
Maria: also toggling feature flag to force original batching: `feature.toggle inference.batch.v2=false`
Devin: can we just reduce max_batch_size on canary pods so they recover instead of full rollback? Maybe hotpatch config map?
Samir: we can hotpatch configmap but some pods already OOM and restart loop. Safer to abort until we confirm fix.
Joan: we need customer impact comms. Maria/Devin, can you estimate affected customers + whether any enterprise SLA breached?
Devin: early estimate: 3 paying customers with heavy streaming usage saw increased error rate; no confirmed SLA breach yet — latency/5xx SLO may be impacted, opening a short incident page for comms.
Maria: abort finished per deploy-bot. `deploy-bot: rollout rl-2026-03-15-09 abort complete, traffic shifted back to rl-2026-02-27-01 (stable).` Traffic weight now 0% to inference-r1.
deploy-bot: Canary group inference-r1 marked FOR_INSPECTION. Instances will remain until manual cleanup.
Samir: I'm collecting heap dumps from healthy pods and crashed ones (where possible). Will run leak detection on the new batching path.
Joan: good. Action items: (1) SRE to keep canary group quarantined and monitor for residual 5xx (Samir), (2) Eng to prepare hotfix switching batching back to safe defaults (Devin), (3) Incident lead to prepare customer comms and PSAT if needed (Maria).
Maria: assigning incident lead now. I'll draft comms and post status to #status. Quick note: no rollback to prod was necessary beyond abort; stable rollout resumed.
Devin: I can reproduce locally with long sequence tokens + batch_size 128 — memory spike. Will prepare minimal patch to clamp batch size to 32 and add safety cap.
Samir: capturing prometheus query snapshots and pod-level oom traces, posting links in the ticket.
Joan: TL;DR for ops: abort executed, canary traffic removed, investigations underway, customer impact limited but possible. If anyone needs to escalate to SEs for customer outreach ping me.
Maria: handing off to follow-on shift at 09:19 UTC — Samir will carry remediation. I'll remain available for comms. :white_check_mark:
Samir: taking handoff. Will update every 15m and attach triage notes.
deploy-bot: Incident thread closed for immediate paging; monitoring alerts still active — create follow-up ticket for postmortem once root cause confirmed.
Maria: thanks everyone. I'll start the incident record and include timeline + commands used.
Joan: add remediation checklist: add mem caps, safety clamp, alert sensitivity review, and add canary abort threshold lowering to trigger earlier next time.
Samir: noted. Posting heap dump links and initial findings in the ticket.
Maria: end of thread update: abort + traffic switch executed at 3345678921, customer outreach prepared (standby), follow-up RFO will be scheduled.
